name: Czech Amber Lager
description: Polotmavé — the 'half-dark' lager sitting between Czech pale and Czech dark. Caramel and Saaz hops, decoction-rich, and almost unknown outside Bohemia.
funFact: Czech beer law grades lagers by original gravity rather than colour or strength, and polotmavé is a recognised category in its own right — a distinction most brewing countries never made.

serve.how: Pour hard down the middle to raise a thick, creamy head — Czech service treats foam as part of the drink, not a byproduct. Serve a touch warmer than a mass-market lager so the caramel malt and the peppery Saaz character both register. If you can get it on a side-pull tap, order it with a dense wet foam cap and drink through it.

composition.summary: A decoction-mashed amber lager balancing caramel malt against Czech Saaz hops.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: Bohemian floor-malted barley with caramel and Munich malts.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: Saaz, in generous late additions for spice rather than bitterness.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: Czech lager yeast, fermented cold and lagered for weeks.

components.label: Other
components.detail: Extremely soft Bohemian water, which is why the bitterness lands round.

composition.process: Double or triple decoction mashing builds the malt depth, followed by cold fermentation and a long cold lagering.

name: Kvass
description: Fermented rye bread, barely alcoholic, sold from street tankers all summer. Sour, sweet and bready — a soft drink by law and a beer by method.
funFact: Kvass is classified as a soft drink across most of Eastern Europe because it usually finishes under 1.2% ABV, which is how it stayed legal and ubiquitous through every temperance campaign.

serve.how: Serve very cold in a tall glass, straight from the fridge or the tanker. Expect a hazy brown pour with a fine, short-lived foam and a distinctly sour-sweet bread aroma. Drink it fast on a hot day — it is a thirst-quencher rather than a sipper, and it flattens quickly once poured.

composition.summary: A low-alcohol lactic ferment of rye bread and water, sweetened and drunk young.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: Rye bread or rye malt, often toasted dark before steeping.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: A mixed yeast and lactic culture that leaves it sour and barely alcoholic.

components.label: Other
components.detail: Sugar or raisins to feed the ferment and round the finish.

composition.process: Toasted rye bread is steeped, sweetened and fermented briefly with a mixed culture, then chilled and drunk within days.
